title: Numerical experience with solving MPECs as NLPs
contribution: Shows on the new 137-problem MacMPEC library that MPECs reformulated as NLPs (with z1'z2 <= 0 and slacks) are solved robustly by SQP solvers (filterMPEC 0 catastrophic failures, SNOPT 1), better than interior-point solvers and at least competitive with special-purpose MPEC solvers.
problem_entry: Contests the received verdict that MFCQ failure (unbounded multipliers) and disappointing past experience rule out NLP solvers for MPECs, using the strong-stationarity/KKT equivalence of [19] (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: No new algorithm: careful NLP formulation (slacks, z1'z2 <= 0, relaxed complementarity linearization with restoration) plus a reliable filter-SQP solver behind an AMPL complements interface (filterMPEC) suffices (pp. 1, 3, 5-6).
assumptions: MPEC form (1.1) with smooth data; recalled theory needs MPEC-LICQ and consistent QPs (known for vertical complementarity); NLP solvers assume a CQ, so failures are expected without MFCQ (pp. 3, 9).
proof_devices: two-variable example min z1+z2, 0<=z1 perp z2>=0: z1z2=0 gives iterates 2^-k z(0) (linear), z1z2<=0 converges in one step (p. 3)
explicit construction of the unbounded multiplier ray and minimal multiplier (2.2), recalled from [19] (pp. 2-3)
hand analysis of the pathological instance dempe: limit x=0 violates MFCQ and is not B-stationary (pp. 11-12)
experiments: 137 MacMPEC problems, filterMPEC/KNITRO/LOQO/SNOPT on NEOS; catastrophic vs soft failure taxonomy (Table 2, p. 9); cause-removal reruns with z1'z2 <= 1e-2 (Tables 3-4, pp. 10-12); iteration and CPU performance profiles with failures as asymptote (pp. 12-14); multiplier-size profile (Fig. 3, pp. 13-15); tentative comparisons with published MPEC-solver iteration counts (Tables 5-7, pp. 15-17).
positioning: Builds on Fletcher-Leyffer-Ralph-Scholtes [19] and Anitescu [1]; surveys smoothing, penalty, Fischer-Burmeister SQP, PIPA, implicit programming; directly corrects Conn et al. and Ferris-Pang on the LANCELOT/LUBRIF failure attribution (pp. 3-4, 10); casts SQP as the benchmark for MPEC solvers (p. 18).
writing: Time-stamped comparative claim in the abstract ('at present', p. 1); hedges concentrated on literature comparisons (tentative, pp. 14-17) and causal attributions; theory recalled only to explain numbers (pp. 3, 12).
limits_future: Perturbation (3.4) properties under investigation (p. 6); one complementarity form not handled by the interface (p. 5); literature comparisons on non-identical instances (p. 15); linear convergence to B-stationary points when no strongly stationary point exists (p. 14); IPM improvements and more comparisons planned (pp. 13, 17-18).

method_links.note: NLP base (filterSQP, filter) carried into MPECs through an AMPL interface; key idea is off-the-shelf NLP solvers
MacMPEC launched with classification scheme, comments, references, plots, online random generator, contributor acknowledgements
'at present' stamp, written failure taxonomy, failures penalized in profiles, iteration and CPU meters with rationale, literature comparisons labelled tentative
baselines are NEOS solvers at defaults and published iteration counts, not self-built baselines at best settings
z1'z2<=0 and slacks as formulation fixes; LUBRIF misattribution; relaxation rerun before blaming MFCQ; dempe failure attributed to formulation; water models re-cast from binaries to complementarity
two-variable instance with closed-form iterates shows linear convergence of the equality formulation; PIPA non-convergence cited from NA/208
own SQP solver extended through a thin interface with minor changes and negligible overhead

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: failed IPM instances rerun with complementarity relaxed to <= 1e-2; LOQO still fails 11 of 20, KNITRO solves 13 of 19, so failures are not solely due to MFCQ
relative complementarity-multiplier size profiled on the subset where all solvers agree; IPM multipliers orders of magnitude larger, curves track the iteration profile

transferable: Rerun only the failing instances with the suspected cause removed and tabulate per instance before attributing failures (Tables 3-4, pp. 10-12).
Split failures by exit reason (catastrophic vs locally infeasible) and penalize only catastrophic ones in performance profiles (pp. 9, 12).
Use both iteration and CPU performance profiles and state what each isolates (p. 12).
Profile a theory-predicted quantity (minimal multiplier) on the agreement subset to explain a performance gap (Fig. 3, p. 13).
For comparisons with published numbers: publish the instance generator, map problem names, argue comparable per-iteration work, label the comparison tentative (pp. 14-17).
Motivate a formulation choice with a two-variable example whose iterates are in closed form (p. 3).
Give library problems a classification string recording origin and structural type so conclusions can be drawn per class (p. 7).

quotes.text: The failure of knitro is a failure of the problem formulation, rather than of the method.
Interior point methods are less robust, failing on about 15 % of problems.
